correctness.rationale: Independently re-ran inputs/artifacts/census.py: reproduced 364 triples, 26 types, uniform orbit 14, DFT-vs-eigvalsh max 2.26e-14, Fourier residuals <=5.55e-14, 12/26 two-sided Ramanujan, 20/26 one-sided, best (1,2,7) at 3.87666977 vs runner-up (1,2,11) at 3.90598165 margin 0.02931>1/40, 26/26 distinct charpolys, min energy gap 0.02578, min Linf 0.55397. Independent stdlib+cmath re-derivation confirmed canon list exactly and all orbit sizes 14. Independent 80-digit mpmath (cos-sum) confirmed tightest Ramanujan boundary (1,3,12) at 4.46967145 vs RB 4.47213595 (margin -0.002464, Ramanujan) and (1,4,7) at 4.56264103 (defect +0.0905, non-Ramanujan), winner/runner-up margins, and full energy ordering with min gap 0.0257866 for (1,2,4)/(1,8,12). Sympy exact charpoly check confirmed all 26 monic, trace 0, x^27 coeff -87 (Tr A^2=174) and pairwise distinct. Turner prime-order multiplier quotient correctly applied; Paley-29 calibration eigenvalues correct. DRAFT Sec.6 honestly labels spectral inequalities/energies as dual-method numerical evidence (margins >>1e-14) vs exact census/charpoly inequality as combinatorial proof; numerical margins are decisive (smallest Ramanujan-boundary distance 0.00246 is 11 orders above discrepancy, cross-validated at 80 digits). No essential inference, boundary, or computation failed.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Hirano-Katata-Yamasaki arXiv:1310.2130 gives asymptotic valency bound guaranteeing odd circulants Ramanujan with restricted exceptional families, not a per-type (29,6) defect census or minimal-defect witness. Minac et al. arXiv:2212.02005 gives generalized-Paley spectra/infinite Ramanujan families/Cheeger bounds, different family and question. Ilic-Basic arXiv:1104.4261 (integral/gcd circulants) and Louis arXiv:1508.02348 (1,gamma two-generator) treat disjoint object classes (prime-order 6-regular circulants are non-integral, irrational DFT spectra, three symmetric pairs). Conde et al. arXiv:2408.07200 proves even-order singularly-cospectral constructions and that two singularly cospectral circulants on odd prime vertices are isomorphic. Since cospectrality implies singular cospectrality, this general theorem implies the (29,6) cospectral partition must be singleton-dominated given distinct multiplier types, so the *shape* (26 singletons) is implied; but it does not record any (29,6) polynomial, energy, defect, or ranking, and does not imply equienergetic distinctness (energy equality strictly weaker than singular cospectrality) nor the Ramanujan dichotomy. No source found records fixed-(29,6) multiplier-quotiented Ramanujan dichotomy, defect spectrum, best-expander witness, or explicit polynomial/energy table.

value.rationale: Strongest headline is self-contained and independently retrievable: fixed-(n,d)=(29,6) multiplier-quotiented census (26 types), full two-sided Ramanujan dichotomy (12/26), unique best-expander (1,2,7) with rational separation >1/40, plus exact reference data (26 distinct integer charpolys, 26 distinct energies with min gap 0.0258, per-type lam2/maxabs/defect/gap/energy table). Stratum is natural and motivated before computation (prime Paley order n=29, smallest nontrivial even valency d=6 above 4-regular, Alon-Boppana/expander benchmarking, valency-bound literature leaves per-type census open; Paley-29 demoted to normalized calibration, eliminating degree-driven predictability). Value not known or mechanically implied (except cospectral-singleton shape implied by Conde, but explicit polynomials/energies/defects/ranking are not), and future circulant-expander selection can reasonably need the precise witness and table. Not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration: structural dichotomy plus separated ranking plus separating invariants. Per narrow-datum rule, one exact order/witness/table is not disqualified by form alone.

residual_risks: Spectral inequalities and energy distinctness rest on dual-method floating-point plus 80-digit cross-check, not interval arithmetic; margins (0.00246 boundary, 0.02578 energy, 0.02931 ranking) are 9-12 orders above observed discrepancies, so flip risk is negligible but not formally enclosed.
DRAFT/research_report state smallest margin as 0.0258/0.029, omitting the tighter 0.00246 Ramanujan-boundary distance for (1,3,12); noted here for honesty, still decisive.
Cospectral-singleton shape is a corollary of Conde+Turner; novelty of cospectral part lies only in explicit polynomials/table, while equienergetic distinctness and defect ranking remain non-implied.
Isomorphism quotient relies on Turner's prime-order theorem (standard) plus exact orbit computation; connectedness uses primality of 29.
